requirements.original: ObjectReference "." send "(" TemplateInstance ")" [ to Address ]
requirements.canonical: The `send` operation has the syntax ObjectReference "." `send` "(" TemplateInstance ")" [ `to` Address ].
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.1 -- ObjectReference "." send "(" TemplateInstance ")" [ to Address ]

requirements.original: NOTE: _Address may be an AddressRef, a list of AddressRef-s or "all component"._
requirements.canonical: The Address in the `to` clause of a `send` operation MAY be an AddressRef, a list of AddressRef items or `all component`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.1 -- NOTE: _Address may be an AddressRef, a list of AddressRef-s or "all component"._

requirements.original: The send operation places a message on an outgoing message port.
requirements.canonical: The `send` operation places a message on an outgoing message port.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.1 -- The send operation places a message on an outgoing message port.

requirements.original: The message may be specified by referencing a defined template or can be defined as an in-line template.
requirements.canonical: The message of a `send` operation MAY be specified by referencing a defined template or as an in-line template.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.1 -- The message may be specified by referencing a defined template or can be defined as an in-line template.

requirements.original: Unicast, multicast and broadcast communication can be determined by the optional to clause in the send operation.
requirements.canonical: The optional `to` clause of a `send` operation CAN determine unicast, multicast or broadcast communication.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.1 -- Unicast, multicast and broadcast communication can be determined by the optional to clause in the send operation.

requirements.original: A to clause can be omitted in case of a one-to-one connection where unicast communication is used and the message receiver is uniquely determined by the test system structure.
requirements.canonical: The `to` clause of a `send` operation MAY be omitted in a one-to-one connection where unicast communication is used and the message receiver is uniquely determined by the test system structure.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.1 -- A to clause can be omitted in case of a one-to-one connection where unicast communication is used and the message receiver is uniquely determined by the test system structure.

requirements.original: Unicast communication is specified, if the to clause addresses one communication partner only.
requirements.canonical: A `send` operation uses unicast communication if the `to` clause addresses only one communication partner.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.1 -- Unicast communication is specified, if the to clause addresses one communication partner only.

requirements.original: Multicast communication is used, if the to clause includes a list of communication partners.
requirements.canonical: A `send` operation uses multicast communication if the `to` clause includes a list of communication partners.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.1 -- Multicast communication is used, if the to clause includes a list of communication partners.

requirements.original: Broadcast is defined by using the to clause with all component keyword.
requirements.canonical: A `send` operation uses broadcast communication if the `to` clause uses the `all component` keyword.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.1 -- Broadcast is defined by using the to clause with all component keyword.

requirements.original: a) The TemplateInstance (and all parts of it) shall have a specific value i.e. the use of matching mechanisms such as AnyValue is not allowed.
requirements.canonical: The TemplateInstance of a `send` operation, and all parts of it, SHALL have a specific value.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.1 -- a) The TemplateInstance (and all parts of it) shall have a specific value i.e. the use of matching mechanisms such as AnyValue is not allowed.

requirements.original: a) The TemplateInstance (and all parts of it) shall have a specific value i.e. the use of matching mechanisms such as AnyValue is not allowed.
requirements.canonical: Matching mechanisms such as AnyValue SHALL NOT be used in the TemplateInstance of a `send` operation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.1 -- a) The TemplateInstance (and all parts of it) shall have a specific value i.e. the use of matching mechanisms such as AnyValue is not allowed.

requirements.original: b) When defining the message in-line, the optional type part shall be used if there is ambiguity of the type of the message being sent.
requirements.canonical: When the message of a `send` operation is defined in-line and the type of the message is ambiguous, the optional type part of the in-line template SHALL be used.
requirements.condition: the message is defined in-line and its type is ambiguous
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.1 -- b) When defining the message in-line, the optional type part shall be used if there is ambiguity of the type of the message being sent.

requirements.original: c) The send operation shall only be used on message-based ports and the type of the template to be sent shall be in the list of outgoing types of the port type definition.
requirements.canonical: The `send` operation SHALL only be used on message-based ports.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.1 -- c) The send operation shall only be used on message-based ports and the type of the template to be sent shall be in the list of outgoing types of the port type definition.

requirements.original: c) The send operation shall only be used on message-based ports and the type of the template to be sent shall be in the list of outgoing types of the port type definition.
requirements.canonical: The type of the template sent by a `send` operation SHALL be in the list of outgoing types of the port type definition.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.1 -- c) The send operation shall only be used on message-based ports and the type of the template to be sent shall be in the list of outgoing types of the port type definition.

requirements.original: d) A to clause shall be present in case of one-to-many connections.
requirements.canonical: A `send` operation SHALL contain a `to` clause in case of one-to-many connections.
requirements.condition: the port has a one-to-many connection
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.1 -- d) A to clause shall be present in case of one-to-many connections.

requirements.original: e) All AddressRef items in the to clause shall be of type address, component or of the address type bound to the port type (see clause 6.2.9) of the port instance referenced in the send operation.
requirements.canonical: Every AddressRef item in the `to` clause of a `send` operation SHALL be of type `address`, of a component type, or of the address type bound to the port type of the port instance referenced in the `send` operation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.1 -- e) All AddressRef items in the to clause shall be of type address, component or of the address type bound to the port type (see clause 6.2.9) of the port instance referenced in the send operation.

requirements.original: No AddressRef in the to clause shall contain the special value null at the time of the operation.
requirements.canonical: No AddressRef in the `to` clause of a `send` operation SHALL contain the special value `null` at the time of the operation.

ambiguity.issue: The consequence of a null AddressRef at runtime is not stated; chosen reading: it is a runtime error (test case error).
readings: Executing a `send` operation whose `to` clause contains a `null` AddressRef SHALL cause a test case error.
A `send` operation whose `to` clause contains a `null` AddressRef is undefined behaviour left to the tool.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.1 -- No AddressRef in the to clause shall contain the special value null at the time of the operation.

requirements.original: f) Applying a send operation to an unmapped or disconnected port shall cause a test case error.
requirements.canonical: Applying a `send` operation to an unmapped or disconnected port SHALL cause a test case error.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.1 -- f) Applying a send operation to an unmapped or disconnected port shall cause a test case error.

requirements.original: g) The ObjectReference shall be of a port type.
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a `send` operation SHALL be of a port type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.1 -- g) The ObjectReference shall be of a port type.

requirements.original: h) _TemplateInstance shall be of a data type._
requirements.canonical: The TemplateInstance of a `send` operation SHALL be of a data type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.1 -- h) _TemplateInstance shall be of a data type._

requirements.original: [ @nodefault ] ( ObjectReference | any port | any from PortArrayRef ) "." receive [ "(" TemplateInstance ")" ] [ from Address ] [ "->" [ value ( ValueRef| ( "(" { ValueRef[ ":=" [ @decoded [ "(" Expression ")" ] ] FieldOrTypeReference ][","] } ")" ) ) ] [ sender ValueRef] [ @index value ValueRef] ]
requirements.canonical: The `receive` operation has the syntax [`@nodefault`] (ObjectReference | `any port` | `any from` PortArrayRef) "." `receive` ["(" TemplateInstance ")"] [`from` Address] ["->" [`value` (ValueRef | "(" {ValueRef [":=" [`@decoded` ["(" Expression ")"]] FieldOrTypeReference] [","]} ")")] [`sender` ValueRef] [`@index value` ValueRef]].

examples.text: any port.receive(mw_myMessage);

requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- [ @nodefault ] ( ObjectReference | any port | any from PortArrayRef ) "." receive [ "(" TemplateInstance ")" ] [ from Address ] [ "->" [ value ( ValueRef| ( "(" { ValueRef[ ":=" [ @decoded [ "(" Expression ")" ] ] FieldOrTypeReference ][","] } ")" ) ) ] [ sender ValueRef] [ @index value ValueRef] ]

requirements.original: NOTE 1: _Address may be an AddressRef, a list of AddressRef-s or "any component"._
requirements.canonical: The Address in the `from` clause of a `receive` operation MAY be an AddressRef, a list of AddressRefs or `any component`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- NOTE 1: _Address may be an AddressRef, a list of AddressRef-s or "any component"._

requirements.original: The message may be specified by referencing a defined template or can be defined as an in-line template.
requirements.canonical: The message to be received by a `receive` operation MAY be specified by referencing a defined template or MAY be defined as an in-line template.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- The message may be specified by referencing a defined template or can be defined as an in-line template.

requirements.original: The receive operation removes the top message from the associated incoming port queue if, and only if, that top message satisfies all the matching criteria associated with the receive operation.
requirements.canonical: The `receive` operation removes the top message from the associated incoming port queue if, and only if, that top message satisfies all the matching criteria associated with the `receive` operation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- The receive operation removes the top message from the associated incoming port queue if, and only if, that top message satisfies all the matching criteria associated with the receive operation.

requirements.original: If the match is not successful, the top message shall not be removed from the port queue i.e. if the receive operation is used as an alternative of an alt statement and it is not successful, the execution of alt statement shall continue with its next alternative.
requirements.canonical: If the match is not successful, the `receive` operation SHALL NOT remove the top message from the port queue.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- If the match is not successful, the top message shall not be removed from the port queue i.e. if the receive operation is used as an alternative of an alt statement and it is not successful, the execution of alt statement shall continue with its next alternative.

requirements.original: If the match is not successful, the top message shall not be removed from the port queue i.e. if the receive operation is used as an alternative of an alt statement and it is not successful, the execution of alt statement shall continue with its next alternative.
requirements.canonical: If a `receive` operation used as an alternative of an `alt` statement is not successful, the execution of the `alt` statement SHALL continue with its next alternative.
requirements.condition: the receive operation is an alternative of an alt statement and is not successful
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- If the match is not successful, the top message shall not be removed from the port queue i.e. if the receive operation is used as an alternative of an alt statement and it is not successful, the execution of alt statement shall continue with its next alternative.

requirements.original: The matching criteria are related to the type and value of the message to be received.
requirements.canonical: The matching criteria of a `receive` operation are related to the type and value of the message to be received.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- The matching criteria are related to the type and value of the message to be received.

requirements.original: The type and value of the message to be received are determined by the argument of the receive operation, i.e. may either be derived from the defined template or be specified in-line.
requirements.canonical: The type and value of the message to be received are determined by the argument of the `receive` operation, derived either from a defined template or from an in-line template.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- The type and value of the message to be received are determined by the argument of the receive operation, i.e. may either be derived from the defined template or be specified in-line.

requirements.original: An optional type field in the matching criteria to the receive operation shall be used to avoid any ambiguity of the type of the value being received.
requirements.canonical: The optional type part of the matching criteria of a `receive` operation SHALL be used to avoid any ambiguity of the type of the value being received.

ambiguity.issue: 'type field' is used for the optional Type ':' prefix of the in-line template, which restriction a) calls 'type part'; 'field' could be confused with a record field.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- An optional type field in the matching criteria to the receive operation shall be used to avoid any ambiguity of the type of the value being received.

requirements.original: NOTE 2: Encoding attributes also participate in matching in an implicit way, by preventing the decoder to produce an abstract value from the received message encoded in a different way than specified by the attributes.
requirements.canonical: Encoding attributes participate implicitly in matching by preventing the decoder from producing an abstract value from a received message encoded differently than specified by the attributes.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- NOTE 2: Encoding attributes also participate in matching in an implicit way, by preventing the decoder to produce an abstract value from the received message encoded in a different way than specified by the attributes.

requirements.original: In the case of one-to-many connections the receive operation may be restricted to a certain communication partner.
requirements.canonical: In the case of one-to-many connections, the `receive` operation MAY be restricted to a certain communication partner.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- In the case of one-to-many connections the receive operation may be restricted to a certain communication partner.

requirements.original: This restriction shall be denoted using the from keyword followed by a specification of an address or component reference, a list of address or component references or any component.
requirements.canonical: The restriction of a `receive` operation to a communication partner SHALL be denoted using the `from` keyword followed by an address or component reference, a list of address or component references, or `any component`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- This restriction shall be denoted using the from keyword followed by a specification of an address or component reference, a list of address or component references or any component.

requirements.original: NOTE 3: The one-to-one connection is considered to be a simple case of the one-to-many connections and allows the usage of the from-clause.
requirements.canonical: A one-to-one connection is considered a simple case of a one-to-many connection, so the `from` clause MAY also be used for a `receive` operation on a one-to-one connection.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- NOTE 3: The one-to-one connection is considered to be a simple case of the one-to-many connections and allows the usage of the from-clause.

requirements.original: If the match is successful, the value is removed from the port queue and/or parts of this value can be stored in variables or formal parameters.
requirements.canonical: If the match is successful, the `receive` operation removes the received message from the port queue.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- If the match is successful, the value is removed from the port queue and/or parts of this value can be stored in variables or formal parameters.

requirements.original: If the match is successful, the value is removed from the port queue and/or parts of this value can be stored in variables or formal parameters.
requirements.canonical: If the match is successful, the received value or parts of it CAN be stored in variables or formal parameters.

ambiguity.issue: 'is removed from the port queue and/or parts of this value can be stored' mixes the always-happening removal with the optional storing; the 'and/or' scope is unclear. Chosen reading: removal always happens, storing is optional.
readings: If the match is successful, the message is removed from the port queue and the whole value or parts of it CAN additionally be stored in variables or formal parameters.
If the match is successful, either the message is removed from the port queue or parts of it are stored, or both.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- If the match is successful, the value is removed from the port queue and/or parts of this value can be stored in variables or formal parameters.

requirements.original: This is denoted by the symbol '->' and the keyword value.
requirements.canonical: Storing the received message or parts of it is denoted by the symbol `->` followed by the keyword `value`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- This is denoted by the symbol '->' and the keyword value.

requirements.original: When the keyword value is followed by a name of a variable or formal parameter, the whole received message shall be stored in the variable or formal parameter.
requirements.canonical: When the keyword `value` is followed by the name of a variable or formal parameter, the whole received message SHALL be stored in that variable or formal parameter.
requirements.condition: value is followed by a single variable or formal parameter name
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- When the keyword value is followed by a name of a variable or formal parameter, the whole received message shall be stored in the variable or formal parameter.

requirements.original: The variable or formal parameter shall be type compatible with the received message.
requirements.canonical: A variable or formal parameter following the keyword `value` SHALL be type compatible with the received message.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- The variable or formal parameter shall be type compatible with the received message.

requirements.original: When the keyword value is followed by a list enframed by a pair of parentheses, the whole received message and/or one or more parts of it can be stored.
requirements.canonical: When the keyword `value` is followed by a parenthesized list, the whole received message and/or one or more parts of it CAN be stored.
requirements.condition: value is followed by a list enframed by parentheses
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- When the keyword value is followed by a list enframed by a pair of parentheses, the whole received message and/or one or more parts of it can be stored.

requirements.original: For each list element that consists only of a variable or formal parameter name the whole message shall be stored in that variable or formal parameter.
requirements.canonical: For each element of a `value` redirect list that consists only of a variable or formal parameter name, the whole message SHALL be stored in that variable or formal parameter.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- For each list element that consists only of a variable or formal parameter name the whole message shall be stored in that variable or formal parameter.

requirements.original: The type of the variable or formal parameter shall be compatible with the type of the message.
requirements.canonical: A variable or formal parameter that is a list element consisting only of a name in a `value` redirect list SHALL be of a type compatible with the type of the message.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- The type of the variable or formal parameter shall be compatible with the type of the message.

requirements.original: Each assignment notation member of the list allows storing the value of the field or element of the received message, which is referenced on the right hand side of the assignment notation (:=), in the variable or formal parameter on the left hand side.
requirements.canonical: Each assignment notation member of a `value` redirect list stores the value of the field or element of the received message referenced on the right hand side of `:=` in the variable or formal parameter on the left hand side.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- Each assignment notation member of the list allows storing the value of the field or element of the received message, which is referenced on the right hand side of the assignment notation (:=), in the variable or formal parameter on the left hand side.

requirements.original: The variable or formal parameter shall be type compatible with the type of the referenced field or element.
requirements.canonical: A variable or formal parameter on the left hand side of an assignment notation member of a `value` redirect list SHALL be type compatible with the type of the referenced field or element.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- The variable or formal parameter shall be type compatible with the type of the referenced field or element.

requirements.original: When assigning individual fields of a message, encoded payload fields can be decoded prior to assignment using the @decoded modifier.
requirements.canonical: When assigning individual fields of a received message, encoded payload fields MAY be decoded prior to assignment using the `@decoded` modifier.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- When assigning individual fields of a message, encoded payload fields can be decoded prior to assignment using the @decoded modifier.

requirements.original: In this case, the referenced field on the right hand side of the assignment shall be one of the bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring or universal charstring types.
requirements.canonical: When the `@decoded` modifier is used, the referenced field on the right hand side of the assignment SHALL be of the bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring or universal charstring type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- In this case, the referenced field on the right hand side of the assignment shall be one of the bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring or universal charstring types.

requirements.original: It shall be decoded into a value of the same type as the variable on the left hand side of the assignment.
requirements.canonical: A field referenced with the `@decoded` modifier SHALL be decoded into a value of the same type as the variable on the left hand side of the assignment.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- It shall be decoded into a value of the same type as the variable on the left hand side of the assignment.

requirements.original: Failure of this decoding shall cause a test case error.
requirements.canonical: Failure of the decoding of a field referenced with the `@decoded` modifier SHALL cause a test case error.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- Failure of this decoding shall cause a test case error.

requirements.original: In case the referenced field is of the universal `charstring type, the @decoded` clause can contain an optional parameter defining the encoding format.
requirements.canonical: If the referenced field is of the universal charstring type, the `@decoded` clause MAY contain an optional parameter defining the encoding format.
requirements.condition: the referenced field is of universal charstring type
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- In case the referenced field is of the universal `charstring type, the @decoded` clause can contain an optional parameter defining the encoding format.

requirements.original: The parameter shall be of the charstring type and it shall contain one of the strings allowed for the decvalue_unichar function (specified in clause C.5.4).
requirements.canonical: The encoding format parameter of the `@decoded` clause SHALL be of the charstring type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- The parameter shall be of the charstring type and it shall contain one of the strings allowed for the decvalue_unichar function (specified in clause C.5.4).

requirements.original: The parameter shall be of the charstring type and it shall contain one of the strings allowed for the decvalue_unichar function (specified in clause C.5.4).
requirements.canonical: The encoding format parameter of the `@decoded` clause SHALL contain one of the strings allowed for the `decvalue_unichar` function.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- The parameter shall be of the charstring type and it shall contain one of the strings allowed for the decvalue_unichar function (specified in clause C.5.4).

requirements.original: Any other value shall cause an error.
requirements.canonical: An encoding format parameter of the `@decoded` clause with a value not allowed for `decvalue_unichar` SHALL cause an error.

ambiguity.issue: The kind of error is not specified.
readings: A disallowed encoding format value SHALL cause a test case error at runtime.
A disallowed encoding format value SHALL cause a compile-time error when it is known statically, and a test case error otherwise.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- Any other value shall cause an error.

requirements.original: In case the referenced field is not a universal **charstring, the optional** parameter shall not be present.
requirements.canonical: If the referenced field is not of the universal charstring type, the optional encoding format parameter of the `@decoded` clause SHALL NOT be present.
requirements.condition: the referenced field is not of universal charstring type
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- In case the referenced field is not a universal **charstring, the optional** parameter shall not be present.

requirements.original: It is also possible to retrieve and store the component reference or address of the sender of a message.
requirements.canonical: The component reference or address of the sender of a received message CAN be retrieved and stored.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- It is also possible to retrieve and store the component reference or address of the sender of a message.

requirements.original: This is denoted by the keyword sender.
requirements.canonical: Storing the sender of a received message is denoted by the keyword `sender`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- This is denoted by the keyword sender.

requirements.original: When the message is received on a connected port, only the component reference is stored in the following the sender keyword, but the test system shall internally store the component name too, if any (to be used in logging).
requirements.canonical: When the message is received on a connected port, only the component reference is stored in the variable following the `sender` keyword.
requirements.condition: the message is received on a connected port

ambiguity.issue: The sentence is garbled ('stored in the following the sender keyword'); the noun 'variable or formal parameter' is missing.

improper_terms.used: stored in the following the sender keyword
improper_terms.proper: stored in the variable or formal parameter following the sender keyword

requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- When the message is received on a connected port, only the component reference is stored in the following the sender keyword, but the test system shall internally store the component name too, if any (to be used in logging).

requirements.original: A receive operation with no argument list for the type and value matching criteria of the message to be received shall remove the message on the top of the incoming port queue (if any) if all other matching criteria are fulfilled.
requirements.canonical: A `receive` operation with no argument for the type and value matching criteria SHALL remove the message on the top of the incoming port queue, if any, if all other matching criteria are fulfilled.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- A receive operation with no argument list for the type and value matching criteria of the message to be received shall remove the message on the top of the incoming port queue (if any) if all other matching criteria are fulfilled.

requirements.original: To receive a message on any port, use the any port keywords.
requirements.canonical: The `any port` keywords MAY be used with the `receive` operation to receive a message on any port.

examples.text: any port.receive(mw_myMessage);

requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- To receive a message on any port, use the any port keywords.

requirements.original: To receive a message on any port from a specific port array, use the any from PortArrayRef syntax where PortArrayRef shall be a reference to a port array identifier.
requirements.canonical: The `any from` PortArrayRef construct MAY be used with the `receive` operation to receive a message on any port of a specific port array.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- To receive a message on any port from a specific port array, use the any from PortArrayRef syntax where PortArrayRef shall be a reference to a port array identifier.

requirements.original: To receive a message on any port from a specific port array, use the any from PortArrayRef syntax where PortArrayRef shall be a reference to a port array identifier.
requirements.canonical: The PortArrayRef in an `any from` PortArrayRef construct SHALL be a reference to a port array identifier.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- To receive a message on any port from a specific port array, use the any from PortArrayRef syntax where PortArrayRef shall be a reference to a port array identifier.

requirements.original: It is also possible to store the index of a port in a singledimensional port array at which the operation was successful to a variable of type integer or, in case of multi-dimensional port arrays the index of the successful port to an integer array or record of integer variable.
requirements.canonical: The index of the port in a single-dimensional port array at which the `receive` operation was successful MAY be stored in a variable of type integer.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.2 -- It is also possible to store the index of a port in a singledimensional port array at which the operation was successful to a variable of type integer or, in case of multi-dimensional port arrays the index of the successful port to an integer array or record of integer variable.
